summary: For the unit-volume spherical shell density rho_R=1_{R<=|x|<=r_R} in R^3, every one-dimensional linear projection has density cap <=1/(2R), the gradient density of |x|^2 has cap 1/8, and E||grad q||^{-1}<=1/(2R), but ||p_{|X|^2}||_inf=2pi r_R>=2pi R. Thus arbitrary-joint coarea cannot be rescued merely by imposing all one-dimensional projection caps. This is not a product-law/QFORM counterexample.
